title: Real-Time Patient Dashboard Pipeline
challenge: The patient monitoring dashboard was slow to load because real-time data streaming was tightly coupled to dashboard rendering. Clinicians could not get timely patient status updates.
action: Designed and implemented a Kafka → AWS S3 decoupling pipeline that separated the streaming layer from the rendering layer. Built a Spring Boot microservice to consume Kafka topics, process and store data in S3, and serve it asynchronously to the React frontend.
result: 70% reduction in dashboard load time, sub-second latency for live vitals, and zero data loss during peak load.

title: Apache Camel → Spring Boot Migration
challenge: A legacy Apache Camel integration process was resource-intensive, hard to maintain, and bottlenecking several clinical data flows.
action: Systematically mapped every Camel route and rebuilt them as Spring Boot microservices with clean REST APIs and a React frontend, adding proper error handling, logging and monitoring along the way.
result: 98% improvement in API efficiency, materially lower resource consumption, and a codebase the team could actually maintain.

title: End-to-End Observability Stack
challenge: Production incidents took hours to diagnose — there was no centralised observability across the distributed clinical system.
action: Stood up a full observability stack: Prometheus for metrics, Grafana dashboards, Loki for log aggregation, Tempo for distributed tracing, OpenTelemetry instrumentation and CloudWatch for AWS-level monitoring.
result: 30–40% reduction in Mean Time To Resolution. Incidents that previously took hours were identified in minutes.

title: Mentoring and Engineering Standards
challenge: Junior developers were not following backend best practices, producing inconsistent code quality and longer delivery cycles.
action: Wrote the team's coding standards, ran weekly code review sessions, introduced microservices design patterns, and paired with each junior developer on their first production feature.
result: 20% improvement in team delivery efficiency, measurably better code quality, and two juniors promoted to mid-level within six months.

title: Complexity-Aware LLM Routing with Failover
challenge: Every AI feature depended on external LLM providers. A single provider outage meant total service failure for paying users.
action: Built a complexity-aware LLM routing layer that detects provider failure and falls over through a chain — DeepInfra → Groq → Together AI — picking model size per task complexity.
result: Near-zero downtime on LLM-dependent features; 99%+ uptime maintained through multiple upstream provider outages.

title: Async Worker Architecture on Postgres
challenge: AI media generation tasks take 30–120 seconds. Running them synchronously would block API responses and wreck the user experience.
action: Built six async background workers using PostgreSQL's FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for job queuing — no Redis or RabbitMQ needed. Each worker owns a task type with its own fallback chain (e.g. Gathos → DeepInfra → Replicate for video).
result: All long-running tasks became non-blocking with SSE progress tracking, and failed jobs auto-refund credits through atomic SQL transactions.

title: Model Context Protocol Integration Layer
challenge: AI agents operated in isolation — they had no access to the user's real-world data, so responses were generic.
action: Built a full MCP integration layer with per-user authenticated connections to Gmail, Google Calendar, GitHub, Notion, Slack and Postgres, so each user's agents run against their live data context.
result: Agents became dramatically more useful — calendar-aware scheduling, inbox-aware communication, code-aware development assistance — and it became the platform's key differentiator.

title: Atomic Credit Ledger
challenge: A multi-tenant SaaS with 11 feature pricing tiers needs a bulletproof credit system — any double-spend or unrefunded failed job costs money and trust.
action: Built an atomic credit ledger on PostgreSQL transactions. Every debit and refund commits or rolls back as a unit; failed background jobs trigger a compensating refund transaction automatically.
result: Zero double-spend incidents, automatic refunds within seconds of any job failure, and a full audit trail for every credit movement.

title: Azure AKS Microservices Platform
challenge: Eeko.ai needed to move from a monolith to a scalable microservices architecture on Azure to serve a growing SMB customer base across subscription plans.
action: Designed and delivered six Spring Boot microservices (masterdata, design-processing, design-rendering, event-processing, subscription, notification) on Azure AKS with Azure MySQL and Blob Storage, plus a WhatsApp Business API notification pipeline built on Spring Batch.
result: The platform handled concurrent design generation and notification delivery across customers, with zero-downtime deployments via an ArgoCD GitOps pipeline.

title: TimescaleDB Market Data Pipeline
challenge: Collecting real-time order book depth — thousands of price levels updated every second — needs specialised time-series infrastructure. Laptop storage ran out within weeks.
action: Migrated collection to a VPS (Ubuntu 24.04, 8 cores, 31 GB RAM) on TimescaleDB with systemd-managed collectors for Databento (MES futures tick data) and Binance (crypto order book depth), solving the pg_dump hypertable chunk problem with a COPY-based workaround.
result: Storage runway went from 3 months to 183 months, collectors survive reboots, and three instruments stream simultaneously with 275 GB free.

title: Custom ICT Backtesting Engine
challenge: Commercial backtesting tools do not support ICT methodology — no order flow, no volume profile, no position blocks with risk-reward visualisation.
action: Built a backtesting engine on top of lightweight-charts with an absolute-positioned SVG overlay for drawing tools, custom hit-detection maths for interactive drawings, simulated order execution and equity curve tracking.
result: The first backtesting tool that natively supports ICT methodology with full order flow visualisation, enabling proper pre- and post-trade analysis.

title: Maternal-Fetal Monitoring Integration
challenge: Connecting proprietary maternal-fetal monitoring hardware to an EMR system and a clinical frontend required complex data transformation across multiple protocols.
action: Built Java Spring Boot integration services bridging the hardware devices, the EMR system and the clinical dashboard — handling format transformation, real-time streaming and error recovery.
result: Clinical staff monitored mother and baby vitals in real time with reliable data integrity, in hospital environments where accuracy is life-critical.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent Incident Response
company: AnnaRakshak AI (Google Build with AI hackathon)
challenge: District agriculture offices detect crop-price collapses manually, taking 85-170 minutes from anomaly to a verification-ready report — far too slow to protect farmers from a crash already underway.
action: Built a deterministic anomaly detector over public AGMARKNET mandi prices (flagging moves of +/-40% against the median of the previous 30 prices), then layered three Vertex AI agents via Google ADK — investigation, evidence review, coordination — with read-only tools that draft case summaries, field-verification tasks and Marathi/English farmer notices but cannot change case state or send anything. Enforced role-based approvals, evidence-confirmed hypotheses, auto-superseded drafts, and an append-only audit log that records denied attempts.
result: Cut detection-to-verification-ready-report from an estimated 85-170 minutes to about a minute, and caught a real -42.1% tomato price crash at APMC Nagpur on 16 Sep 2026.

title: Zero-Loss Market Data Migration
challenge: A production VPS migration had to move millions of tick-level market data rows without losing a single event — and pg_dump was silently dropping TimescaleDB hypertable chunks.
action: Diagnosed the silent pg_dump hypertable bug, switched to a COPY-based transfer path, and migrated the full dataset with verification at each stage.
result: Moved 221K+ bars, 1.78M flow events and 824K depth ticks with zero data loss.

title: Production Database Exposure, Found and Fixed
challenge: The production deployment had PostgreSQL and Redis ports bound to 0.0.0.0 — reachable from the public internet on a VPS with live customer data.
action: Identified the exposure during a deployment review, documented the SSH-tunnel remediation path, rebound the services to localhost and hardened the deployment.
result: Closed a live data-exposure path before any incident, and documented the fix so the pattern would not recur.
